advances: The marked quotient point is fixed across all levels and cap normals. The tail budget uses actual raw depths.

proof:
The level $j$ is exactly $\pi_t(C\cap\{j-k\le t\le j\})$. In the full range the two cutoffs are redundant. For $j<l$ with $j\ge\lceil a_0\rceil$, the lower cutoff is below $a_0$; for $j=k+s>r$ with $s\le\lfloor b_0\rfloor$, the upper cutoff is above $b_0$. These ranges exhaust the integer levels because the projected $t$ interval is $[a_0,b_0+k]$.

Restrict a through-$(j,y)$ cap to each level. If the $t$ coefficient is nonnegative, all full levels at or above $j$ and all right tails retain at least the quotient through-$y$ cap. If the coefficient is nonpositive, use the levels at or below $j$ and all left tails. A vanishing quotient normal gives whole favorable traces, whose mass is at least their depth. For $y$ off a tail the corresponding depth contribution is zero. Parallel translation from a containing cap to a through-point cap only decreases mass. This proves the two budgets. In the variable $j-l$, their minimum is their constant mean minus $Q$ times distance from their crossing. A crossing in $[0,N-1]$ is within $1/2$ of the nearest allowed level, giving the stated bound.

The total mass is $N\mu_{n-1,d}(T)$ plus the sum of actual tail masses. For example, if $Q=\beta\mu_{n-1,d}(T)$, the balance bound holds, and $L+R$ is at least $\beta$ times the sum of tail masses, the resulting depth is at least half $\beta$ times the total mass. For the planar hull of $(0,-2),(0,-1),(1,1),(1,2)$, the unique deepest mark of $T=[-2,2]$ is $0$. The two actual tails are $[-2,-1]$ and $[1,2]$, each of positive length and depth zero at $0$.
statement:
Let $C$ be nonempty compact convex in primitive unimodular coordinates $(t,w,x)$, let $T=\pi_t C$, and use the actual mixed measures in each ambient space. Suppose $T$ has positive quotient mass. Put $a_0=\min_C t$, $b_0=\max_C t$. For any integer $k\ge\lceil b_0\rceil-\lfloor a_0\rfloor$, set $l=\lceil b_0\rceil$, $r=k+\lfloor a_0\rfloor$, $N=r-l+1$. The integer levels of $C+[0,k]e_t$ consist of full copies of $T$ for $l\le t\le r$, left tails $T^-_s=\pi_t(C\cap\{t\le s\})$ at $t=s$ for $\lceil a_0\rceil\le s<l$, and right tails $T^+_s=\pi_t(C\cap\{t\ge s\})$ at $t=k+s$ for $\lfloor a_0\rfloor<s\le\lfloor b_0\rfloor$.

For an actual quotient mark $y$, let $Q=D_T(y)$, $L=\sum_sD_{T^-_s}(y)$, $R=\sum_sD_{T^+_s}(y)$, where $D$ is raw closed-halfspace depth, zero off the convex set and equal to mass in a zero-dimensional quotient. For every integer $l\le j\le r$,
$$
D_{C+[0,k]e_t}(j,y)\ge \min\{(j-l+1)Q+L,(r-j+1)Q+R\}.
$$
When $Q>0$, the maximum of the right-hand side over these levels is
$$
\frac{(N+1)Q+L+R}{2}-Q\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac{N-1}{2}+\frac{R-L}{2Q},\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\right).
$$
If $|R-L|\le(N-1)Q$ this is at least $(NQ+L+R)/2$. Positive tail mass alone need not give positive credit at the deepest quotient mark.
title: Depth in full extruded levels with actual tail credit
